propositions.text: The claimant is a citizen of Djibouti claiming protection under section 96 and paragraphs 97(1)(a) and (b) of IRPA.
propositions.quote: The refugee protection claimant, XXXX XXXX XXXX, is a citizen of Djibouti. She is claiming protection under section 96 and paragraphs 97(1)(a) and (b) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (hereafter the IRPA).

paragraphs.summary: The claimant is a Djibouti citizen claiming protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1)(a) and (b), court states.

propositions.text: The panel determines the claimant is not a Convention refugee under section 96 or a person in need of protection under subsection 97(1) of IRPA.
propositions.quote: the panel determines that she is not a "Convention refugee" under section 96 of the IRPA, or a "person in need of protection" within the meaning of subsection 97(1) of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The panel decides the claimant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection under IRPA, court states.

propositions.text: The claimant fears domestic violence from her husband, whom her parents forced her to marry without consent.
propositions.quote: The claimant fears being a victim of domestic violence at the hands of her husband, whom her parents forced her to marry without her consent.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges fear of domestic violence from a forced marriage husband.

propositions.text: Before marriage, claimant worked at a savings and credit union and had a secret boyfriend for three years.
propositions.quote: Before she got married, she worked as an XXXX XXXX at a XXXX XXXX, namely the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX [savings and credit union]. She had already been in a relationship with another man, XXXX XXXX, for three years.

propositions.text: She did not tell her parents about her boyfriend because it was taboo.
propositions.quote: She did not tell her parents that she had a boyfriend because it was taboo.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant worked at a savings union and hid her boyfriend from parents due to taboo, claimant states.

propositions.text: In late 2015, claimant's father told her to marry a man named XXXX, shocking her; wedding was set for XXXX 2015.
propositions.quote: It was not until a few days later her father told her she had to marry a man named XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX When she heard the news, she was in shock. The wedding was to take place on XXXX XXXX, 2015.

propositions.text: She told her father about her relationship, but he threatened to disown her if she refused the arranged marriage.
propositions.quote: She explained to her father that she was already in a relationship. Her father threatened to disown her if she did not marry the man he had chosen.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant says her father forced marriage and threatened disownment if she refused, shocking her.

propositions.text: One week before meeting future husband's family, claimant fled to a friend's house; later visited hospitalized father who threatened her.
propositions.quote: At the end of XXXX, one week before she was supposed to meet her future husband's family, the refugee protection claimant fled to friend's house. One week later, she learned that her father had been hospitalized. She went to visit him. He told her that if he died, it would be her fault.

propositions.text: Out of fear of losing her father, claimant agreed to marry the man.
propositions.quote: She agreed to be married out of fear of losing her father.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant fled before meeting husband's family but agreed to marry fearing her hospitalized father's death, claimant says.

propositions.text: Marriage started well but deteriorated after 3-4 months with husband mistreating and beating her and attacking adopted nephew.
propositions.quote: The marriage went well at the beginning. The relationship began to deteriorate after three or four months. The claimant's husband began mistreating her. They fought about the claimant's salary and he beat her. He also attacked her sister's son, whom they had adopted.

propositions.text: Claimant's husband is the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX.
propositions.quote: The claimant's husband is the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant says the husband mistreated her and attacked their adopted nephew after initial good marriage.

propositions.text: In 2016, claimant's sister advised her to flee; claimant obtained a visa and entered Canada claiming refugee protection.
propositions.quote: In XXXX 2016, when she was speaking with her sister who was living in Montréal, her sister told to her flee. She took the steps to obtain a visa, which she obtained on XXXX XXXX, 2016. She went to the United States on XXXX XXXX, 2016. She crossed the Canadian border on November 12, 2016, and she claimed refugee protection.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant fled in 2016 after sister's advice, obtained visa, and claimed refugee protection in Canada.

propositions.text: The Minister intervened on credibility and submitted document M-11 as evidence.
propositions.quote: The Minister intervened on the issue of credibility in this case, submitting document M-11 into evidence.

paragraphs.summary: The Minister challenges claimant's credibility and submits document M-11, respondent states.

propositions.text: The panel considered Guideline 4 on Women Refugee Claimants Fearing Gender-Related Persecution.
propositions.quote: In its decision on this refugee protection claim, the panel took into consideration the Guideline 4: Women Refugee Claimants Fearing Gender-Related Persecution.

paragraphs.summary: The panel considered Guideline 4 on women refugee claimants fearing gender-related persecution, court states.

propositions.text: The panel is satisfied the claimant is a Djibouti citizen based on passport, identity card, and testimony.
propositions.quote: The panel is satisfied as to the claimant's identity as a citizen of Djibouti, as established through a photocopy of her passport, her identity card and her testimony.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds claimant's Djibouti citizenship established by documents and testimony, court finds.

propositions.text: Claimant's testimony was vague with inconsistencies and omissions, especially regarding key dates.
propositions.quote: The claimant's testimony was often vague and it contained several inconsistencies and omissions. For one, the claimant's written account does not mention the key dates in her story.

propositions.text: Claimant had difficulty providing exact months for incidents despite repeated questioning.
propositions.quote: When the panel attempted to obtain more specific dates or the month of the incident, the claimant had great difficulty responding.

propositions.text: Claimant gave inconsistent answers about when husband's behavior changed, citing different months and explaining months are difficult for her.
propositions.quote: For example, when she was asked to specify the month in which her husband's behaviour changed and he hit her for the first time, she stated, [translation] "three months after the wedding and two months after the wedding." With respect to when her husband's behaviour changed, after several questions from the panel she eventually stated that it was in XXXX. Then, she recanted and stated it was August. She explained her error, stating that months are difficult for her.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds claimant's testimony vague and inconsistent on dates, with difficulty specifying months, court finds.

propositions.text: Even giving benefit of doubt on dates, inconsistencies and omissions undermine claimant's credibility.
propositions.quote: Even if the panel were to give the claimant the benefit of the doubt concerning the issues with dates, and considering the difficulties that female victims of domestic violence may have in testifying, the significant inconsistencies and omissions previously noted between her testimony and the documents submitted into evidence do not lead the panel to find that the claimant was credible.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds claimant not credible despite date difficulties due to inconsistencies and omissions, court finds.

propositions.text: Claimant gave vague answers about daily life with husband, undermining probative value of testimony.
propositions.quote: She first gave vague answers such as [translation] "he insulted me, beat me, called me names," but she did not explain the context in which it happened. The panel is of the opinion that all of that undermines the probative value to be given to that part of her testimony.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds claimant's vague answers about husband's behavior undermine testimony's probative value, court finds.

propositions.text: There is a major inconsistency in husband's name and birth date between American visa application, BOC Form, and marriage certificate.
propositions.quote: Correspondence with American authorities, a document submitted by the Minister, contains information about the refugee protection claimant in her application for an American visa. It indicates that her husband's name is XXXX XXXX XXXX, born on XXXX XXXX, 1984. However, her BOC Form indicates that her husband's name is XXXX XXXX XXXX, born in 1987. As well, the marriage certificate indicates that his name is XXXX XXXX XXXX, born in 1991.

paragraphs.summary: The panel notes major inconsistencies in husband's name and birth date across documents, court finds.

propositions.text: At hearing start, claimant corrected husband's birth date on BOC Form from 1987 to 1991.
propositions.quote: At the beginning of the hearing, the claimant made several corrections to her BOC Form, including a correction to her husband's birth date at question 5a). It first stated 1987, which she changed to XXXX XXXX, 1991.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant corrected husband's birth date on BOC Form at hearing start, claimant states.

propositions.text: Panel is not satisfied with claimant's explanation for birth date correction, noting she wrote her full birth date elsewhere.
propositions.quote: The panel is not satisfied with the claimant's explanations. The panel notes that the claimant's date of birth is XXXX XXXX, 1987, and that it appears in full on all of the forms; she never wrote just the year.

propositions.text: Panel believes claimant would have written full birth date if she had mistakenly written her own instead of husband's.
propositions.quote: The panel is of the opinion that if the claimant had truly made a mistake and wrote her date of birth, as opposed to that of her husband, she would have written her full date of birth.

paragraphs.summary: The panel rejects claimant's explanation for birth date error, finding it unlikely she wrote only the year by mistake, court finds.

propositions.text: Claimant said a third party filled out American visa form in a rush, explaining errors in husband's info.
propositions.quote: She explained that a third party had filled out the American visa application form for her. It was someone she had paid at an Internet cafe. She stated that she was in a hurry when she applied for the visa because there was a deadline approaching.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant explains third party filled American visa form hurriedly, causing errors, claimant states.

propositions.text: Panel is unsatisfied with claimant's explanation, noting importance of accurate info in fleeing for life.
propositions.quote: The panel is completely unsatisfied with the claimant's explanations. For one, the panel notes that this claim was made with the aim of fleeing Djibouti because she fears for her life. Therefore, it is crucial that this claim be accepted.

propositions.text: Panel notes another incorrect piece of information in the correspondence, further undermining claimant's credibility.
propositions.quote: In addition, the panel notes that another piece of information in this correspondence is incorrect.

paragraphs.summary: The panel rejects claimant's explanation, emphasizing need for accurate info and noting further errors, court finds.

propositions.text: Due to significant credibility issues about husband's identity, panel does not believe claimant's allegations forming basis of claim.
propositions.quote: Given the significant credibility issues raised with respect to the identity of the claimant's husband, which the panel considers to be central to her refugee protection claim, the panel does not believe the claimant's allegations that form the basis of her claim.

paragraphs.summary: The panel disbelieves claimant's allegations due to major credibility issues about husband's identity, court concludes.

propositions.text: There is a contradiction and an omission in the claimant's written account about her fear and seeking help.
propositions.quote: In paragraph 17 of her written account, the claimant states the following [translation] "From that day on, I was so afraid that I didn't dare tell anyone about what happened to me." However, in one of the corrections,6 she states that the following should be added to paragraph 17 [translation] "I did, however, go see the Union des femmes de Djibouti...."

paragraphs.summary: The court finds a contradiction and omission in the claimant's written account about her fear and seeking help.

propositions.text: The claimant's explanations for the contradiction were incomprehensible and inconsistent regarding threats and memory.
propositions.quote: When the panel confronted her with that contradiction, her explanations were explications were incomprehensible. To begin, she stated that her husband had threatened her if she spoke to anyone of what had happened. Then, she stated that she was telling the truth here. She was questioned about the fact that, in her BOC Form, she indicated the opposite of what she was stating during her testimony. She answered that her problems had made her forget.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant's explanations for the contradiction incomprehensible and inconsistent.

propositions.text: The panel is unsatisfied with the claimant's explanations and does not believe her allegations due to undermined credibility.
propositions.quote: The panel is unsatisfied with the claimant's explanations. All of that undermines her credibility, to the point where the panel does not believe her allegations.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant's credibility undermined and does not believe her allegations.

propositions.text: The panel concludes there is an overall lack of credibility in the claimant's story and key allegations.
propositions.quote: Considering the preceding, the panel concludes that there is an overall lack of credibility with respect to the claimant's story and key allegations.

propositions.text: Due to lack of credibility, the panel attaches no probative value to other submitted documents, including the marriage certificate.
propositions.quote: Because of that lack of credibility, the panel attaches no probative value to the other documents submitted into evidence, including the marriage certificate.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes an overall lack of credibility and attaches no probative value to other documents including the marriage certificate.

propositions.text: The claimant did not establish a serious possibility of persecution on Convention grounds.
propositions.quote: Having assessed all of the evidence, the panel concludes that the claimant did not establish that there is a "serious possibility" that she will face persecution on one of the Convention grounds.

propositions.text: The claimant failed to demonstrate on a balance of probabilities a risk of torture, death, or cruel treatment if returned to Djibouti.
propositions.quote: She also failed to demonstrate, on a balance of probabilities, that she would be subjected to a danger of torture, a risk to her life or a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment if she were to return to Djibouti.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the claimant failed to prove serious persecution or risk of torture, death, or cruel treatment if returned to Djibouti.

propositions.text: The refugee protection claim is rejected.
propositions.quote: The refugee protection claim filed by XXXX XXXX XXXX is rejected.

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects the refugee protection claim.
